title: The canonical enveloping map for a central simple algebra is bijective
statement: Let $K$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional nonzero associative unital $K$-algebra whose center is the image of $K$ and whose only two-sided ideals are $0$ and $A$. Write $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ for the opposite algebra. The canonical $K$-algebra homomorphism $A\otimes_K A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{End}_K(A)$, sending $a\otimes b^{\mathrm{op}}$ to the linear map $v\mapsto avb$, is bijective.

source.place: Tag 074I, proof; tensor simplicity in Tag 074G

proof.text: The opposite algebra is central simple. Tag 074G gives that its tensor product with A is simple. The canonical map sends a tensor a⊗op(b) to left multiplication by a followed by right multiplication by b, and is a unital K-algebra homomorphism. Its kernel is a two-sided ideal, hence zero or the whole domain. The target is nonzero and the map preserves one, so the kernel is zero. Thus the map is injective.

The dimensions of the tensor product and of End_K(A) both equal (dim_K A)^2. The canonical map is K-linear; its injectivity and the dimension equality imply surjectivity. Together these give bijectivity of the actual map, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism.
